respōnsum

noun, second declension

an answer, a reply

In this lexicon

  • answer

    the recommended word · classical · Quint. 1.5.36: cum respōnsum ab interrogante dissentit; Traupman 28: alicui respōnsum reddō

Notes

  1. 1respondeō, respōnsum: short e in re- (Lewis & Short rē-spondeo, rēsponsum). The prefix is re-, from Proto-Italic *wre, “back” (de Vaan 516, s.v. re-, red-). Lewis & Short writes rē- before sc, sp and st, and only there. Its article on the prefix gives rĕ, with a by-form rĕd-, and puts the poets’ rēdūcō, rēlātum down to “the suppression of the d”; the long mark before s and a consonant seems to rest on the same idea, as its dī-scindō from dis- does. Bennett (The Latin Language §48) rejects that lengthening for ascendō, distinguō, suspiciō as “an untenable theory of compensatory lengthening”, and Lewis’s own Elementary Latin Dictionary (1890) prints re-spondeō. Traupman writes respondēre too. Ruling: re- short before sc, sp, st.
